posts.text:
Some of the best data available on psychedelic use and policy come from RAND.

Researchers have studied the options—and the trade-offs—as some states begin to ease access to psychedelics. bit.ly/3QCyxaC

The race toward artificial general intelligence poses serious national security risks.

In a new paper, RAND experts offer a strategic approach that could help the United States navigate the transition to an AGI world. bit.ly/426fWq8
Here's how RAND's Robert Lempert is using his expertise to help his community rebuild after the 2025 L.A. fires: piped.video/watch?v=URRwHM3v…
As AI systems assume more decisionmaking roles in government, the economy, and society, a question emerges: Will humans retain the capacity to shape collective outcomes? bit.ly/4tnsXat

Could deep sea mining break China's grip on critical minerals?

Here's what our research says about the challenges facing Washington: bit.ly/4tYcp9d
New study examines what could happen if Indiana—typically considered one of the more restrictive U.S. states—changes its approach to cannabis. bit.ly/49aNiYv

Millions of young people are disconnected—out of school, out of work, and not in career training.

This has costly implications for individuals, taxpayers, and society.

🎧 New episode of Policy Minded: bit.ly/3P8aPmd

What do people misunderstand about psychedelics? Do Americans support legalizing these drugs? And what can be learned from how cannabis policy has evolved?

New Q&A with RAND's @BeauKilmer: bit.ly/421JXXV
This new paper introduces "AGI Rideout," a strategy for reducing strategic risk and promoting stability in the transition to artificial general intelligence. bit.ly/48wvWoW

RAND's Robert Lempert talks to the @latimes about getting security system notifications that his house was burning while he evacuated from the 2025 Palisades Fire, what's needed to help the community rebuild, and how he's putting his expertise to work: piped.video/watch?v=URRwHM3v…

President Trump moved this month to expedite research and increase access to some psychedelic substances for the treatment of serious mental health disorders.

In this new Q&A, RAND's Beau Kilmer discusses psychedelics, policy, and public opinion:
bit.ly/4uj60pj

AI is already changing the strategic environment around chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats.

This research agenda highlights what to study *now* to reduce risks while also leveraging AI's potential to reinforce security. bit.ly/4tn82V1

Ground robots face several obstacles to taking on infantry combat, says @RANDEurope's Jacob Parakilas.

"The first is, quite literally, obstacles." bit.ly/48gQJwy

"We need to find alternative sources of these critical minerals that don't involve China. This is an all-of-government, all-hands effort. Seabed mining is one way we might accomplish it." bit.ly/4tS6diG

More than 4 million young people in the U.S. are out of school, out of work, and not in career training.

What does that mean for their futures—and for society as a whole?

New episode of Policy Minded: bit.ly/3Qu9kPO

National security and technology leader Victoria Coleman, financial executive William Downe, and nuclear security expert Lisa Gordon-Hagerty have been elected to RAND's Board of Trustees. bit.ly/4e2eU5A

Robert Lempert is a researcher at RAND who works to help communities understand and manage climate risks. He also has a personal connection to disaster, losing his home in the 2025 L.A. fires.

Hear about his experience in this @latimes interview: piped.video/watch?v=URRwHM3v…
Jacob Parakilas of @RANDEurope discusses how Ukraine uses military ground robotics for critical support on the battlefield. bit.ly/4cVD9RU
New paper outlines a research agenda for understanding AI's impact on chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risk. bit.ly/48bErWj
